definition: The strongest common English swear word and its euphemistic or censored spellings, in any grammatical form.
Vulgar word for feces or nonsense, including compound forms like bullshit. Not offensive when literally discussing livestock manure in a farming context, though that is rare in lyrics.
Vulgar insult for a woman or a complaint verb. Not offensive when referring to a female dog in a veterinary context.
Vulgar word for buttocks or a stupid person. Not offensive when meaning a donkey in a biblical or farming context.
Insult for an unpleasant man; originally means a child born out of wedlock, which sense is dated but still flagged by most families.
Mild curse expressing anger. Not offensive in the literal religious sense of divine condemnation.
Mild curse or intensifier ('what the hell', 'hella' as West-Coast slang for 'very'). Not offensive when it names the actual place of damnation, e.g. in a hymn or sermon.
Mild vulgar word for feces, junk or bad quality.
Vulgar word for urine or, in British slang, anger/mockery. Not flagged in neutral medical or animal-care contexts.
Vulgar word for penis or a jerk. Not offensive as the name Dick or the slang term for a detective in period fiction.
Vulgar word for penis. Not offensive for a rooster or the hammer of a gun in historical contexts.
Among the most offensive English words; a vulgar term for female genitalia or a person.
Vulgar British insult meaning idiot or female genitalia.
Vulgar British insult derived from masturbation.
Extremely vulgar compound insult; 'mf' and 'mofo' are its abbreviations.
Vulgar insult for a contemptible man or slang for penis. Not offensive for the literal meaning of a small puncture or thorn.
British vulgar word for testicles or nonsense.
British mild-to-vulgar insult; also a verb for anal sex. Mild when used affectionately ('poor bugger').
Insult for an obnoxious person, from the hygiene product.
Vulgar compound insult.
Euphemistic stand-in for 'fucking' as an intensifier; many families still want it muted.
Censored or abbreviated forms of 'what the fuck'.
Vulgar in sexual phrases ('suck my'); merely crude when meaning 'is bad' ('this sucks'). Not offensive for literal suction, a lollipop, or breastfeeding.
Vulgar slang for sexual intercourse or cheating someone. Not offensive for the hardware fastener.
Vulgar word for female breasts.
Vulgar word for female genitalia or an insult for weakness. Not offensive when clearly meaning a cat.
Slang for female breasts; 'melons' and 'jugs' are euphemisms that are only flagged when clearly used for breasts.
Pornography; 'corn' is a common euphemism-misspelling used to evade filters.
Explicit references to sexual activity. Not offensive in clinical, educational or biological senses.
Oral sex; 'head' and 'dome' are slang for it and only flagged when that sense is clear, since 'head' usually means the body part.
Manual sexual stimulation.
Slang for semen or orgasm; 'nut' is only flagged in the sexual sense, not for food or hardware. 'Come' is not a variant: it is a normal word.
Group sex.
Derogatory word for a promiscuous person, usually a woman.
Prostitute or an insult for promiscuity; spelled 'hoe' in rap slang. Not offensive for the garden tool when clearly meant.
Acronym slur ('that hoe over there') for a woman judged promiscuous.
Erotic dancer; 'pole' is only flagged in the strip-club sense, not for flagpoles or the North Pole.
Sexually suggestive buttocks-focused dancing.
A call or invitation for casual sex. 'Booty' alone is only flagged when clearly sexual, not for pirate treasure.
Slang for having sex ('smash that'). Not offensive for literal breaking, the video game, or a hit song.
In phrases like 'clap them cheeks', slang for sex or shooting. Not offensive for applause or a round of applause.
Numeral slang for a mutual oral sex position. Not offensive as an ordinary number.
Subscription platform strongly associated with explicit content.
In a sexual context, slang for oral sex. Not offensive when meaning dining at a restaurant.
In 'ride me'-type phrases, slang for sex. Not offensive for transport, horses or a musical ride cymbal.
Sex slang for ejaculating on a face. Not offensive for the spa treatment.
Sex slang for internal ejaculation. The dessert 'cream pie' is not flagged unless clearly used sexually.
Slang for sex or an erection ('boner'). Not offensive for skeletons, chicken bones or bone broth.
Slang for cannabis; 'herb' and 'bud' are only flagged in the cannabis sense, not cooking or flowers.
Cannabis by its standard names.
Slang for cannabis. Not offensive for cookware or plants.
Dated slang for cannabis. Not offensive for lawns or grass the plant.
Slang for drugs (especially heroin historically) but also means 'excellent' in hip-hop. Flag only when referring to actual drugs.
The drug and its slang; 'blow', 'snow' and 'white girl' are only flagged when meaning cocaine, not weather or a person.
Slang for cocaine. Not offensive for Coca-Cola or the fuel coke; context decides.
Crack cocaine and 'crackhead' for an addict. Not offensive for cracks in walls, cracking jokes, or cracking software.
Slang for MDMA/ecstasy. 'Molly' is only flagged as a drug reference, not the woman's name; 'X' and 'E' only when clearly meaning the drug.
The benzodiazepine alprazolam used recreationally; 'bars' and 'xans' are its slang but 'bars' also means rap verses, so context decides.
Prescription opioid oxycodone used recreationally; 'percs' and 'perkies' are its slang.
Recreational codeine-promethazine drink and its slang. 'Lean' is only flagged in this sense, not for leaning or lean meat.
Opiate cough-syrup drug used recreationally in 'lean'.
The opioid and its slang; 'H' is only flagged when clearly meaning the drug.
Methamphetamine and its slang; 'crystal', 'ice' and 'glass' are only flagged when meaning the drug.
The potent opioid; 'fenty' is its street slang and also Rihanna's brand name, so context decides.
LSD and related slang; 'tripping' is only flagged when meaning the drug experience, not stumbling or being foolish. Not offensive for chemistry acids.
Psilocybin mushrooms. 'Mushrooms' is only flagged when clearly meaning the hallucinogen, not food.
Cannabis strain name used as generic slang for strong weed.
Slang for high-grade cannabis, popularized by Dr. Dre's album. Not offensive in the medical sense of chronic illness.
Cannabis-culture number slang. Not offensive as an ordinary number or time.
Being intoxicated on drugs. Not offensive for height, volume or spirits ('flying high' in a general sense is borderline but usually literal altitude).
Intoxicated on cannabis. Not offensive for lapidary stones or biblical stoning punishment (which belongs to violence).
Slang for being high on cannabis. Not offensive for ovens or bread.
Slang for intoxicated or an exciting party. Only flagged when clearly meaning intoxication rather than excitement or lighting.
A cigar hollowed out and refilled with cannabis. Not offensive for blunt honesty or a blunt object.
A cannabis cigarette. Not offensive for body joints, 'joint' meaning a place, or a joint effort.
Inhaling concentrated cannabis oil ('doing dabs'). Not offensive for the dance move or a small amount.
Inhaling powdered drugs through the nose. Not offensive for the laughing sound.
Slang for a drug supplier or connection. Not offensive for electrical plugs or promotional plugs.
Slang for selling drugs or a drug-dealing location. Not offensive for animal traps or trap music as a genre name alone.
Opioid drugs and their common names.
The most severe anti-Black racial slur, including its reclaimed in-group spelling 'nigga' as used in rap. Always flagged regardless of speaker intent.
Slur for a gay man; 'fag' is its short form. Not offensive for the British cigarette slang or a bundle of sticks.
Slur for a lesbian, though partly reclaimed in-group. Not offensive for a dam or embankment.
Slur for a transgender person. Not offensive for an automotive transmission.
Slur for a Chinese or East Asian person. Not offensive for a small dent or a chinking sound.
Slur for an East or Southeast Asian person. Not offensive for slimy residue.
Slur for a Hispanic or Latino person.
Slur for a Jewish person.
Slur for a Mexican immigrant.
Slur for a Mexican or Hispanic person.
Slur for a person who wears a turban or head covering, aimed at Sikhs, Muslims and Arabs.
Racial slur for a Black person. Not offensive for a raccoon.
Slur for a white person. Not offensive for the snack or a Christmas cracker.
Slur for a white person. Not offensive for a honking sound or honky-tonk music.
Latin American term for a foreigner, usually Anglo-American; ranges from neutral to derogatory. Borderline: flag only in clearly derogatory use.
Slur for a Japanese person. Not offensive in 'Jap' as a clipped adjective in old texts, but flag modern usage.
Slur for a Pakistani or South Asian person in British usage.
Considered a slur for Romani people by many; 'gyp' (to cheat) derives from it. Borderline when used for the lifestyle stereotype.
Ableist slur for intellectual disability. Not offensive for the literal meaning 'to slow' in technical or musical ('ritardando') contexts.
Considered a slur by many people with dwarfism. Not offensive in historical contexts naming old product lines or as a size class in sports.
Leetspeak or symbol-substituted spellings of slurs and profanity used to dodge filters; treat them as the base word.
Killing a person in a violent context; 'murk' is slang for murder. Not offensive for 'kill it' (perform well), killing time, or killer apps.
Homicide and its slang 'murda'. Not offensive for 'murder' meaning to outperform ('murdered that beat') unless clearly literal.
Gun violence; 'bust a cap' and 'pop' (in context) are slang for shooting. Not offensive for photography shoots, basketball shots, pop music or taking a shot of a drink.
Firearms and gun slang ('nine', 'strap', 'blicky', 'draco'). Only flagged in weapon senses; 'strap' can also mean a guitar strap, 'chopper' a helicopter.
Ammunition in a violent context. Not offensive for bullet points, silver bullets, or slugs the animal.
Knife violence; 'shank' is slang for a makeshift knife or stabbing. Not offensive for the golf shot or lamb shank.
Graphic gore or injury in context. Not offensive for donating blood, blood relations ('blood brother' can be gang or kin; context decides), or blood orange.
A dead body in a graphic context. Not offensive for 'corpse pose' in yoga or esprit de corps.
Graphic depictions of blood and mutilation. Not offensive for Al Gore or a gored panel in sewing.
Sexual assault. Always flagged when used of people.
Asphyxiation as violence. Not offensive for choking under pressure, a carburetor choke, or choking on food.
Mob killing, strongly tied to racial terror in the US. Not offensive for the surname Lynch.
Mass killing. Not offensive for a lopsided defeat ('massacred the competition') unless described graphically.
Cutting off a head.
Self-killing; flag explicit mentions including slang 'off myself'. Not flagged for 'suicide' as a sports drill name.
Execution by hanging or hanging as a threat. Not offensive for hanging out, hanging pictures or a hangnail.
Cutting a throat or wrists in violent context. Not offensive for a narrow opening or a slit skirt.
Flogging violence when literal; in modern slang it more often means a car ('new whip') or whipping cream. Context decides.
Using God's name as a curse or intensifier.
The name used as an exclamation of shock or anger. Not offensive in worship, quotation of scripture or genuine reference to Jesus.
The name as a casual oath ('Jesus!' 'jeez'). Not offensive when referring to Jesus of Nazareth.
The name as an oath. Not offensive when naming Christ or a Christian.
God's name as an exclamation; 'oh my lord' only when it is the exclamation, not an address to a nobleman.
Compound curse pairing 'holy' with profanity.
Swearing oaths by God or sacred things as slang emphasis ('on God' = 'I swear').
'God-forsaken' used as a curse adjective.
Explicit invocations of divine names in vain, e.g. 'I swear to God' in anger.
Desecrating something sacred; flag only when sacred objects or rites are mocked or profaned.
